note: Paths no script may delete. Enforced by scripts/deliverables.test.mjs.
A DELIVERABLE is an output that a rerun cannot reconstruct. artifacts/ is not one — every
screenshot and report in it is regenerated on demand, which is why it is gitignored and why
scripts clear it freely. The wordlist and the patch are the opposite: once translations are
typed into them the content exists nowhere else, and no amount of rerunning brings it back.
This list exists because shoot.mjs opened with rmSync('artifacts/audit') while the wordlist
owner's 104-row patch was sitting in that directory. Taking screenshots deleted it, and the
run reported success. Per-directory scoping fixed that one script; this stops the next one.
A trailing / means the whole tree.
overwriteNote: A WHOLE-FILE WRITE is destructive too, and it is how a deliverable was actually lost.
emit-blank-rows.mjs rebuilt docs/wordlist-patch.xlsx from scratch and wrote it over the
wordlist owner's copy. Nothing was unlinked, so the delete guard above stayed green; 91
authored translations were gone and the run printed its usual success line.
This list is NARROWER than `paths`, deliberately, and the difference is the point:
- `paths` is about DELETION and covers docs/ wholesale, because deleting a directory of
documentation is never right. It fails closed: a delete whose target the resolver cannot
read is reported, since an unanalysable delete is the one that matters.
- `neverOverwrite` is about CONTENT A HUMAN TYPED. Most of docs/ is regenerated —
lsd-gaps.md is rewritten by two different scripts by design — so covering docs/ wholesale
would report those as violations and the guard would be deleted within a week. It also
only judges FULLY RESOLVED targets: a codemod's `writeFileSync(file)` inside a loop over
src/ resolves to `*` and is not evidence of anything.
That narrowing is a real gap and is written down rather than hidden: a script that computes
the path to the wordlist at runtime can still overwrite it and this will not catch it.

neverOverwrite.why: The source of truth. Every LSD value in the app is generated from it.
The wordlist owner's queue. Translations typed into it exist nowhere else until they are pasted into the wordlist.

mayOverwriteNote: The exemptions, and what earns one: the module READS the file, computes the new content from
what was there, writes, and then RE-READS and verifies — asserting the outcome rather than
the intention that produced it. A failure leaves the original in place.
An exemption list is a real cost, because this is the file someone edits when they want their
script to be special. Two entries, and each one is a verifier.

mayOverwrite.why: Merges blank rows into the patch, then re-reads the written file and asserts no row was dropped, no existing LSD value changed, and every added row is blank — restoring the original bytes if any of the three fails. scripts/lib/patch-merge.test.mjs asserts all three fire, including on a deliberately destructive merge.

Rewrites Kanz doubles in the wordlist in place. Re-reads the patched workbook and checks every row cell by cell against the value it computed, refusing to write on any mismatch or row-count change. Its own comment: 'the outcome, not the intention that produced it'.
